history.sg_progress: The Administration considers this recommendation to be implemented with the promulgation of the policy guideline (OHR/PG/2024/7) of 26 December 2024, which was issued on the basis of lessons learned since the issuance of ST/SGB/2019/3 and ST/IC/2019/15 on flexible working arrangements and their implementation in various contexts, including during the coronavirus disease (COVID-19) pandemic and the “next normal”. The policy guideline provides policy clarifications on key aspects of telecommuting under both flexible working arrangements and alternate working arrangements, including decision-making processes and impacts on benefits and allowances. For flexible working arrangements, and telecommuting in particular, the following elements are reiterated: (a) Flexible working arrangements, including telecommuting outside the duty station, are voluntary agreements requiring prior approval and the establishment of a formal agreement between the staff member and the manager when the arrangement is of a continuous nature. No formal agreement is required in the case of a one-time ad hoc arrangement, though prior approval by the manager is still required; (b) Flexible working arrangements are approved subject to exigencies of service and may be suspended or cancelled at any time by the manager due to exigencies of service or unsatisfactory performance; (c) The policy guideline highlights the maximum duration of telecommuting outside the duty station that may be authorized, including the duration that a head of entity has the authority to approve, and that any approval to telecommute outside the duty station may be granted only for compelling personal reasons. While the Board noted that requests to telecommute for over three days during the workweek accounted for 4.37 per cent of all telecommuting requests, the Administration is of the view that this does not provide a significant basis for keeping this recommendation open. The Administration has reminded entities to comply with the policy and guidance on telecommuting and will continue to stress to entities the need to do so. The Administration therefore requests the closure of this recommendation by the Board based on the policy guidance that has been issued.

history.recommendation_text: The Board recommends that Administration remind entities to comply with the policy and guidance on telecommuting.
history.administration_response: The recommendation was implemented. In accordance with United Nations policy, as set out in the Secretary- General’s bulletin (ST/SGB/2019/3) and the information circular (ST/IC/2019/15) on flexible working arrangements, regular telecommuting within the duty station is limited to a maximum of three days weekly. Exceptions beyond this maximum are allowed only for compelling personal reasons and operational needs, requiring written managerial approval, and do not affect staff benefits. The Office of Human Resources policy guideline (OHR/PG/2024/7) further clarifies the criteria for exceptions and the roles of managers, executive offices and human resources offices. The Office of Human Resources has repeatedly emphasized to entities that telecommuting for more than three days is non-routine and needs full justification, authorization and documentation. Entities must record arrangements in Umoja and conduct regular reviews to ensure consistent policy implementation. The Administration analysed Umoja attendance data to identify cases of excess telecommuting. Such instances are minimal, mostly time-bound and justified by personal or operational needs, therefore complying with the exception rules. With the issuance of the Office of Human Resources policy guideline and ongoing Umoja-based monitoring and compliance reminders, the Administration has fully addressed the Board’s recommendation.
history.board_assessment: Given that the Administration has put in place implementation measures, complemented by the issuance of the Office of Human Resources policy guideline (OHR/PG/2024/7), as well as the monitoring of telecommuting patterns through Umoja attendance data, the Board considers the recommendation to be implemented.
